sources.title: Budget-Friendly Bathroom Renovation Ideas for Modern Style
sources.quote: a basic renovation for a small bathroom (25 to 35 sq. ft.) with simple tiles and standard fittings typically costs around Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 60,000.

notes: Per bathroom, budget tier (basic tiles and fittings; scope varies by source). Cited: NoBroker 'Basic fittings & tiles' ₹40,000–₹70,000 (NoBroker's 3 BHK interior design cost guide for Pune, per bathroom); RealCostIQ budget ₹50,000–₹1,00,000 (national); Comaron basic renovation with new tiles, fittings and waterproofing ₹30,000–₹60,000 for a 6×8 ft bathroom (national); Design Cafe small bathroom (25–35 sq ft) with simple tiles and standard fittings ₹25,000–₹60,000 (national). Range widened to cover all four: ₹25,000–₹1,00,000. Expected = median of the cited publishers' midpoints (one per publisher), rounded to the nearest ₹500 with ties rounded down (midpoints 42,500, 45,000, 55,000, 75,000 → 50,000). The low end reflects small bathrooms; the national sources describe bathrooms of 25–48 sq ft. Components are an editorial split anchored on RealCostIQ (CP fittings, cubicle, geyser and exhaust ~38–39%, sanitaryware ~20%, labour ~18%) and 99acres (labour 20–25% of the total); preparation, repair, transport and waste are labelled assumptions, not sourced. GST: none of these sources says whether its total includes GST; NoBroker and Livspace quote some line items (plumbing, waterproofing) as 'plus 18% GST', so treat the range as GST basis not stated. All figures are labour-included totals per bathroom; Livspace's ₹1.25–₹2 lakh figure excludes tiles and fixtures and is therefore not used.
